Alice (Support): heads up: AcmeMaps escalated — p95/p99 for /v1/generate jumped overnight. p95 ~120ms -> ~850ms, p99 ~400ms -> ~2400ms. They see timeouts and a few 503s. Ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/ticket/789123. Sending logs + sample request.
Ben (Eng Runtime): thx. Any deploys around the window? can we get traces + cache metrics? send grafana links.
Carla (SRE): deploy bot shows a rollout at 1937999000 (small runtime tweak). Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd/runtime-kv-cache — cache hit rate tanked around the same time. KV cache miss rate ~12% -> 78% for hot prefixes. p95 corresponds with miss spikes.
Dan (Infra): looking at node-level logs — eviction churn high on the serving pool. eviction_rate_per_min jumped x6. logs show frequent `cache.delete` for same prefix keys.
Ben (Eng Runtime): can someone paste a sample cache key from logs? suspect key explosion / high cardinality.
Dan (Infra): snippet from runtime log:
```
cache.get key=prompt|model:gpt-2.7|user:12345|prompt_hash:7f3a9c2bd  -> miss
cache.set key=prompt|model:gpt-2.7|user:12345 |prompt_hash: 7f3a9c2bd
```
Notice the space before `|prompt_hash` in some logs — looks like inconsistent normalization.
Frank (ML): oof, if prompt text isn't normalized before hashing then tiny differences (trailing spaces, newline chars, different truncation) create distinct cache keys. That will trash the prefix/KV cache for high-cardinality users.
Ben (Eng Runtime): agreed. Also the runtime used raw `user_id` in the key. That makes keys per-user+prompt — not great for shared prefix caching. We intended to scope by tenant for private deployments, but this is hosted; we should scope by `tenant_group` and prefix-only hash for prompt content.
Alice (Support): AcmeMaps says they started a batch job that reapplied templates yesterday — maybe churned prompt content. They want a mitigation asap, they're seeing degraded UX in production.
Carla (SRE): immediate mitigation options:
- rollback the runtime roll (safer) :arrow_left: but will take 10-15m to cascade.
- enable cache bypass for AcmeMaps so they get stable but slower behavior (no thrash) — toggle via feature flag.
- increase cache admission (eviction pressure) temporarily to buy time.
Ben (Eng Runtime): I'd rather fix key normalization + reduce cardinality. Quick patch:
```
// normalization pseudocode
norm = normalize(prompt)    // trim, collapse whitespace, strip ephemeral tokens
prefix_hash = sha1(norm[0:256])
cache_key = fmt("prefix|model:%s|prefix_hash:%s|scope:tenant_group:%s", model, prefix_hash, tenant_group)
```
Will open PR to normalize and drop user_id from the key for hosted customers. Also add a max-length on the prefix used for cache key.
Dan (Infra): for short-term config I'll bump cache.size from 32gb -> 48gb for the affected serving pool and change eviction_policy from LRU -> segLFU for better protection against scan thrash. Doing now on canary nodes.
DeployBot: Started canary rollout: runtime/key-normalize PR -> https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/412 ✅
Frank (ML): tests: we should add a synthetic load that simulates high prompt variance and assert hit-rate stays >= 70% for hot prefixes.
Ben (Eng Runtime): added repro script to run locally and in staging. snippet:
```
for i in $(seq 1 500); do
  prompt="Search for city $(uuidgen)  "  # trailing spaces + tiny differences
  curl -s -X POST https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d "{\"prompt\": \"$prompt\"}" &
done
```
This reproduces miss storm within ~30s.
Alice (Support): I'll tell AcmeMaps: immediate workarounds: 1) We'll toggle cache bypass for their tenant to avoid thrash (slower but stable). 2) We will apply a short-term credit and escalate to eng. Please confirm ETA so I can update them.
Ben (Eng Runtime): ETA: patch + tests in 40m, canary deploy 10m after, monitor for 30m. If canary looks good we'll roll to remaining nodes. I'll also add metric alerts for `kv_cache.miss_rate > 40%` and `eviction_rate > 3x baseline` on p95 watch.
Carla (SRE): canary up — observing p99 drop on canary replicas from ~2.2s -> ~420ms. Overall pool still noisy while roll continues. Setting incident note.
Dan (Infra): increased cache capacity for affected pool. Eviction pressure down ~60%.
Ben (Eng Runtime): PR merged and rolled to prod: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/commit/9a7f6c2 — key changes: prompt normalization, cap prefix size to 256 bytes, drop per-user keying for hosted tenants, add metrics for key-cardinality.
DeployBot: Rollout completed to 60% at 1938005200, to 100% at 1938005600.
Carla (SRE): post-deploy metrics: p95 ~200-300ms (back to baseline for most traffic), p99 ~320ms. Cache hit rate for hot prefixes increased from 22% -> 76%.
Alice (Support): AcmeMaps confirmed improvements in their environment. They've accepted the credit and will monitor for 24h. I'll keep the ticket open until 24h stable.
Ben (Eng Runtime): follow-ups:
- add unit/integration tests for key normalization
- add a periodic background warmup for top-k prefixes after node restart
- consider segmented cache (hot vs cold) with admission control
- alerting + runbook update for cache thrash (including quick toggle for bypass)
Frank (ML): also add evaluation: ensure normalization doesn't over-collapse meaningful prompt differences. I ran on sample eval set — negligible impact.
Dan (Infra): created infra task to add capacity autoscaler for KV cache (ticket INF-992).
Carla (SRE): closing incident if no regressions in 24h. tagging incident-2026-03-kv-thrash.
Alice (Support): thanks team :clap: — I'll post closure message to customer after 24h. If anything else crops up ping me.
Ben (Eng Runtime): notes saved to runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/kv-cache-thrash
(End of thread)
